captureNotes: An initial shared-Eval obs helper collision raised TypeError before any control mutation. Isolated scripts then performed all native mutations; no service response exists for that failed local call.

Call label register-ondemand-table is an intended test label, not a verified billing fact: preceding call 97 showed ACTIVE PROVISIONED after overlapping billing updates. Followup uses a fresh confirmed PAY_PER_REQUEST table.

The billing-provisioned-active wait expired after 101.359 seconds without ACTIVE. A subsequent reverse UpdateTable returned PAY_PER_REQUEST/UPDATING, but call 97 observed ACTIVE/PROVISIONED; exact eventual resolution of that overlapping reverse request was not established before cleanup.
Poll maxSeconds bounds scheduling; one in-flight CLI request may finish after the stated polling interval deadline.

HTTP status was not independently observed; capture retains AWS CLI JSON outputs/errors, whose timestamps are CLI-rendered ISO strings. Projection update rejection was CLI ParamValidation, not a native service rejection.

nativeFindings.finding: CreateTable returned CREATING; immediate DescribeTable also CREATING; later bounded polls observed ACTIVE. Exact-name duplicate rejected while case-distinct names both existed.
Native admission rejected unused/missing attribute definitions, INCLUDE without NonKeyAttributes, two HASH keys, and LSI partition key unlike table. Existing GSI name creation rejected.

Table and GSI provisioned throughput updates succeeded and were later ACTIVE. Projection inside GSI Update is rejected locally by AWS CLI ParamValidation; no native projection-mutation result is claimed.

PAY_PER_REQUEST creation returned zero provisioned RCU/WCU and explicit billing summary. Initial PROVISIONED creation omitted BillingModeSummary. Table class STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS changed to STANDARD independently.
DescribeTable, UpdateTable, TTL controls and DeleteTable accepted table ARN. A wrong-account ARN returned AccessDeniedException.

ListTables honored nonexistent lexicographic cursors and case ordering; Limit=1 pages used LastEvaluatedTableName when more tables remained; final full one-table page omitted cursor; after-all cursor returned empty TableNames.

Tags preserved empty values. Duplicate tag keys and aws: prefix rejected. Successful tag/untag were initially stale; bounded followup polls observed additions and removal, including removal request with an absent key.

TTL started DISABLED, enable returned specification, next describe observed ENABLED. Repeat enable, attribute replacement, wrong-attribute disable, and immediate correct-attribute disable produced distinct ValidationException messages; no expiration cadence was tested.
AAS rejected missing table and confirmed PAY_PER_REQUEST table. Independent read/write dimensions reused preexisting DynamoDB service-linked role.
AAS bounds drove real table throughput: read minimum raised R2/W1 to R3/W1; write minimum raised to R3/W2; read upper bound reduced to R2/W2.
Deregistering read target removed its scaling policy but retained write target, table and current throughput. Policy-generated alarms were subsequently absent.

DeleteTable succeeded with write target registered, returned DELETING, immediate describe was DELETING and repeated delete was ResourceInUseException. After table became ResourceNotFound, write target still existed until explicit deregistration.
All three created tables have confirmed ResourceNotFound, all owned target inventory is empty, generated alarms are absent, and preexisting service-linked role was unchanged.

uncertainties: Overlapping billing reversal was admitted while previous transition remained UPDATING; reverse request response said PAY_PER_REQUEST, but later ACTIVE description remained PROVISIONED. Exact later resolution before table deletion was not established. Call99 therefore does not establish on-demand admission; call156 does.
Observed timing is experiment-specific and is not an exact service guarantee. TTL enable transitioned too quickly to observe ENABLING; disable could not proceed within short control interval.
No TTL item expiry cadence or utilization-alarm-driven scaling was exercised; AAS bound-driven native throughput changes were exercised.
Projection update admission evidence is CLI-side only. No HTTP statuses were independently observed; fields are not synthesized.

documentationFacts.fact: TTL enable/disable may take up to one hour; repeated updates during the interval can fail; expired item deletion is best effort.
TagResource/UntagResource and ListTagsOfResource are eventually consistent.
Target identity is namespace/resource/dimension. Registration/update adjusts active resource capacity into bounds; DynamoDB supports a service-linked role.
Deregistering a target deletes its associated scaling policies and scheduled actions.
